files.name: deflated_sharpe.py
files.title: Euler–Mascheroni constant, to double precision.
files.summary: Deflated Sharpe Ratio: the haircut a Sharpe owes to the size of the search. PBO answers "is this leaderboard informative?" The Deflated Sharpe Ratio answers a different question that PBO leaves open: **given that N configurations were tried, how much of this particular Sharpe is simply the expected maximum of N draws?** Comparing a best-of-N Sharpe against zero is the mistake.

files.name: gridsim.py
files.title: Jupiter Trigger V2's hard floor. A rung below it is not a small order, it is a
files.summary: Resting-ladder grid simulator — the strategy the extension actually trades. This is deliberately NOT a `Strategy` in the `core.engine` sense. That protocol maps history to one target exposure filled at a bar boundary, and a grid's entire edge comes from **resting limit orders that fill intrabar at known prices**.

files.name: indicators.py
files.title: Multiple of `span` retained when evaluating an exponential recursion. Chosen
files.summary: Trailing-window indicator functions. Every function here takes an array that the caller has ALREADY truncated to bars <= now (a `BarWindow` accessor does this by construction) and returns the value for the latest bar. None of them can see the future, because none of them are ever handed it. Two conventions worth knowing: * Each returns a scalar for the current bar, not a series.

files.name: leverage.py
files.title: Forced-close slippage on top of the liquidation level. 50 bps is an assumption,
files.summary: Low / medium / high margin tiers: run any long/flat strategy as a perp position. A tier is only a leverage multiple plus the venue's cost model. The wrapped strategy decides WHEN to hold exposure; the engine decides what holding it costs at leverage L: open/close fees, slippage, the hourly borrow fee on notional, maintenance margin, and liquidation with an adverse fill and forfeited collateral.

files.name: metrics.py
files.title: metrics
files.summary: Performance metrics with explicitly stated conventions. Ambiguous annualisation is the most common source of a wrong Sharpe ratio, so every convention here is named in the signature and echoed into the report: sample stdev (ddof=1), a 365-day crypto year, and an explicit risk-free rate.

files.name: pairs.py
files.title: pairs
files.summary: Peer-relative-value reversion: trade a cointegrated spread, not a raw price. One mechanism serving two cards. `pairs_cointegration.md` runs it against BTC or ETH, which this repo can fetch keyless; `jlp_vs_sol_relative_value.md` runs it against JLP, whose price history nobody publishes — the code is identical and only the peer series differs.

files.name: perps.py
files.title: perps
files.summary: Jupiter-Perps-style borrow fees, margin, and liquidation. The one thing to get right about this venue: it charges a **borrow fee**, not a funding rate. Consequences encoded here: * Longs and shorts BOTH pay. There is no long-pays-short transfer. * The rate is a product of two non-negative quantities, so it is floor-bounded at zero. No position is ever paid to stay open.

files.name: plotting.py
files.title: plotting
files.summary: Equity-curve and drawdown charts. matplotlib is imported lazily behind a guard so that a missing install degrades to "no charts" rather than failing an otherwise complete run.

files.name: report.py
files.title: Grounding for the multiple-comparisons warning.
files.summary: Comparison reporting, with the caveats the numbers require. A sorted Sharpe table is the most misleading artifact a backtester can emit. Everything here exists to stop that: buy-and-hold is always shown as the baseline, in-sample and out-of-sample are separate columns, and the count of configurations evaluated is printed so a reader can weigh the selection bias.

files.name: scorecard.py
files.title: Component parameters and auxiliary inputs: plain JSON-shaped mappings.
files.summary: Compound five-minute scorecard: score each metric, aggregate into an UP / DOWN / FLAT call. from backtester.core.scorecard import default_config, evaluate, explain, Bars Every component maps visible history to a score in [-1, 1] (+1 = the metric says the next bar closes higher, -1 = lower, 0 = no opinion, NaN = undefined here). Gates map history to "blocked" (no trade, whatever the score says).

files.name: trianglesim.py
files.title: (bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size, quote_time); sizes may be None when the source has none.

A triangle is USD plus two coins A and B with three markets: `A-USD`, `B-USD` and the cross `A-B` (quoted in B per A).

files.name: trigger_conditions.py
files.title: One condition per group in a conjunction: two conditions from the same group
files.summary: Causal trading conditions shared by the trigger miner and `trigger_trade`. Every value at index t is computed from bars 0..t only (trailing windows, EMAs). `research/triggers.py` mines conjunctions of these; `core/strategies/trigger.py` trades them. One implementation keeps the mined edge and the traded edge the same measurement. No I/O here.

files.title: test_candle_gap_audit
files.summary: Gap detection and repair-merge logic in `research/candle_gap_audit.py`. The audit's whole value is the distinction between "this minute was quiet" and "this minute traded and the exchange dropped it", so the tests here pin the mechanics that decision rests on: which bars are reported missing, and that a repaired series replaces the damaged bars rather than accumulating duplicates of them.

files.name: test_cpcv.py
files.title: test_cpcv
files.summary: Known-answer tests for combinatorial purged CV and PBO. The PBO cases are constructed so the correct answer is known by design: a signal set where the in-sample winner always wins out-of-sample must yield PBO ~ 0, and one where in-sample rank carries no information must yield PBO ~ 0.5. Without those two anchors, a PBO implementation can be arbitrarily wrong and still look plausible.

files.summary: The cross-asset CPCV script's pure parts. No test here loads a price file, runs the engine, or writes anywhere under `research/results/`. files.title: Long enough for the 251-bar warm-ups (`ou_reversion`, `hurst_switch`,
files.summary: Tests for the per-bar rule readout in `research/decide.py`. The readout's one substantive claim is that its target exposures are the same numbers the engine would have acted on. Three tests defend it: * **Engine parity.** A recording wrapper captures every `on_bar` return the engine asks for, and the replay must reproduce that sequence exactly, for every registered strategy.

files.name: test_decide_audit.py

files.name: test_deflated_sharpe.py
files.title: test_deflated_sharpe
files.summary: Tests for the Deflated Sharpe Ratio. The first test is the one that matters: it pins the implementation to a figure the source paper states in prose, so the formula cannot drift into something plausible but wrong. Bailey & López de Prado report that at N=1,000 independent trials with unit cross-sectional variance and zero mean, the expected maximum Sharpe is **3.26**.

files.title: test_interpret
files.summary: Tests for the self-explaining sweep output. `interpret()` turns four numbers into the reading a person should take from them. Its most important job is catching the two dangerous misreadings: * a high positive-count with a high PBO ("lots of strategies work!") * a LOW PBO with a low positive-count ("great, rank generalises!") The second is the subtle one, so it gets the most coverage here.

files.name: test_strategy_duplication.py
files.title: test_strategy_duplication
files.summary: `bb_reversion` and `zscore` are one hypothesis counted twice. Found by `research/dso_audit.py`'s S4 pass, which flagged them as posting identical summary scalars on BTC daily, and confirmed by comparing per-bar exposure: on 1,875 BTC daily bars the two strategies took **exactly the same position on every bar**. The reason is algebra, not coincidence.

files.title: Real registry names, so the FAMILY lookups inside the gate are meaningful.
files.summary: The sweep's combination gate, and the measurement it now consults. No test here loads a price file or runs the engine; the gate is pure set logic over a CSV, and `OUT_DIR` is redirected into a tempdir wherever a read could otherwise reach `research/results/` -- which holds published evidence. What is worth pinning is that the three gates genuinely disagree, and disagree in BOTH directions.

files.name: test_textbook_strategies.py

files.summary: Tests for the five mechanisms named by the cited trading guides. Source catalogue: `tradingstrategyresults.json`. Each test targets what the mechanism could get *wrong*: DCA's ramp arithmetic, the PPO's scale invariance (the one property that separates it from MACD), the Fibonacci up-swing order and the turn-up condition, and the swing breakout level excluding its own bar.

The backfill walks a month of trades BACKWARD in pages, folding each page into a running per-bar aggregate. That means a bar's opening trade usually arrives *after* its closing trade, and often in a different page entirely.

files.title: executor — agent rules
files.summary: Guarded spot swaps on Solana through Jupiter. **It signs and sends real transactions from the owner's wallet.** Treat every change as production software. Read the root `CLAUDE.md` "Live on-chain actions" first; its six conditions bind you here too.

files.name: README.md
files.title: executor — guarded Solana swaps
files.summary: The **executor** component of solmargintrader: best-price spot swaps on Solana through Jupiter, behind a semantic transaction verifier, hard rails, a research gate, a dry-run soak and an append-only journal. cd executor

files.name: __init__.py
files.title: __init__
files.summary: executor: a guarded spot-swap executor for Solana (Jupiter). It can move real money; read CLAUDE.md first.

files.name: api.py
files.title: api
files.summary: HTTP surface: `executor api [--port N]`. Stdlib `http.server`; the same access model as extension/tools/api-server.js. GET /v1/health liveness, no auth GET /v1/commands the `list` envelope GET /v1/<command>?a=1 read-only commands, args from the query string POST /v1/<command> any command, args from a JSON object body Command routes return the registry envelope exactly as `registry.dumps` renders i

files.name: cli.py
files.title: cli
files.summary: Command line: `executor quote|swap|status|journal|kill|resume|gates|reconcile|list|call|api`. The CLI prints the registry envelope exactly as the HTTP API returns it (same serializer, byte-identical), and exits 0 when `ok` is true, 1 otherwise, 2 for a usage error.

files.name: config.py
files.title: The reserved strategy id for proving the live path. It is not a trading strategy: the code caps it at
files.summary: Configuration: `~/.executor/config.toml` (or `$EXECUTOR_HOME/config.toml`), created mode 600 with safe defaults. Fail closed: an unknown key, a wrong type, a non-finite or non-positive number, or a file that other users can write is an error. Defaults are the owner's (2026-11-07): max position $25 per strategy, daily loss stop $10.

files.name: engine.py
files.title: engine
files.summary: The swap pipeline. Dry-run and live share every step up to the signature, so dry-run simulates exactly what live would send (the same pattern as liquidity's Rebalancer/Runner). resolve -> quote + independent price -> rails -> /swap -> decode -> VERIFY (static) -> pre-state -> simulate -> VERIFY (economic) ........ dry-run stops here ........

files.name: errors.py
files.title: Envelope error codes. The first five are the same set soltui's registry uses; `refused` and `ambiguous` are
files.summary: Error types. Every refusal carries a code that maps to the envelope `error.code`.

files.name: gates.py
files.title: -- soak ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
files.summary: Pre-live gates, per strategy: a dry-run soak and a research gate. Same pattern as liquidity/src/aero_lp/gates.py. 1. Dry-run soak. A strategy must have run in dry-run for `[gates].soak_hours` (24 h) with at least `[gates].min_dry_runs` fully simulated dry-run swaps before it may go live. Every dry-run swap that passes the whole pipeline credits one tick (`record_dry_run`).

files.name: http.py
files.title: http
files.summary: Minimal HTTP seam so every network client can be tested with recorded fixtures and no live network.

files.name: journal.py
files.title: journal
files.summary: Append-only journal of intents and results: `$EXECUTOR_HOME/journal.jsonl`, mode 600. Every swap that will be sent is written BEFORE sending (`intent`, then `sending` with the signature) and its outcome AFTER (`result`). Lines are only ever appended, each under an exclusive lock and fsynced. State is derived by replaying the file; nothing is rewritten.

files.name: jupiter.py
files.title: jupiter
files.summary: Jupiter Swap API v1 client (quote + swap) and the Jupiter Price API (the independent reference). Verified 2026-11-07 against https://dev.jup.ag/docs/swap/get-quote: base URL `https://api.jup.ag` (key via the `x-api-key` header) and the keyless `https://lite-api.jup.ag`, the host the extension's manifest also lists.

files.name: ledger.py
files.title: ledger
files.summary: Pure accounting over the journal: per-strategy position (cost basis) and realized P&L per UTC day. Only confirmed, on-chain outcomes count. The quote asset is always USDC, so cost and proceeds are exact USDC amounts taken from the transaction itself; the base-asset quantity is the transaction's measured delta.

files.name: lifi.py
files.title: Destination tokens by chain: symbol -> (address, decimals). Native tokens use the zero address.
files.summary: Cross-chain quote, QUOTE ONLY. Nothing here builds, signs or sends a cross-chain transaction. LI.FI's `/v1/quote` answers without an API key (checked 2026-11-07; unauthenticated use is rate limited). It also returns a `transactionRequest`; this module drops it on purpose so that no caller can execute from it.

files.name: quote.py
files.title: quote
files.summary: Quote evaluation: the best route Jupiter finds, checked against an independent price reference. A quote is only usable when (a) every number is present, (b) its price impact is within `max_price_impact_bps`, (c) its implied rate is within `max_price_deviation_bps` of the Jupiter Price API (a separate service and data path from the quote engine), and (d) its slippage cap is within `max_slippage_bps

files.name: rails.py
files.title: rails
files.summary: Rails: every limit an order must pass, as code. A rail documented but not enforced is not a rail. All rails fail closed: a missing price, an unknown side, an unreadable record or a non-finite number is a refusal, never a pass. `check_trade` returns every problem at once so a caller sees the whole picture.

files.name: registry.py
files.title: -- context -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
files.summary: The executor command registry: one set of calls for the CLI and the HTTP API. Every surface calls `dispatch(name, params, surface)`, which validates parameters, applies the confirm gate, runs the handler, wraps the outcome in the response envelope and appends one line to the call log. The surfaces only carry bytes; none holds command logic.

files.name: rpc.py
files.title: rpc
files.summary: Solana JSON-RPC client over the injectable HTTP seam. Read calls retry (bounded, with backoff) because repeating a read is harmless. `send_transaction` NEVER retries: a send that errors or times out has an unknown outcome, and the caller must journal it as such.

files.name: signer.py
files.title: signer
files.summary: Signing key loading. The key is never printed, logged, hashed, copied, or included in an exception message. The file must be a regular file, owned by the current user, with no group or other permission bits (mode 600 or stricter). The same open file descriptor is used for the checks and the read, so the file cannot be swapped in between.

files.name: tokens.py
files.title: The quote asset of every strategy trade: a buy spends it, a sell receives it.
files.summary: Token table and exact amount conversion. Only tokens listed here can ever be traded: decimals come from this table, never from a guess. A mint that is not here is refused even when it is in the config allowlist, because an unknown decimal count turns a $1 order into a $1,000,000 one.

files.name: txverify.py
files.title: --- Program allowlist. Each entry says why the program may appear and what it may do. ---------------------------
files.summary: Semantic transaction verifier: what the extension never had. Runs BEFORE anything is signed. Jupiter's `/swap` returns a serialized transaction. That response is untrusted: a compromised or buggy API could return a transaction that drains the wallet while still "being a swap". Nothing is signed until two layers pass. Layer 1, `check_static` (pure, no network): reads the transaction itself.

files.name: conftest.py
files.title: -- transaction builder ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
files.summary: Shared test machinery: an isolated home, a fixture-backed HTTP seam, an in-memory chain, and a transaction builder. No test here touches the network. Recorded responses live in tests/fixtures (captured from the live services on 2026-11-07); everything else is built in memory.

files.name: README.md
files.title: SolMarginTrader
files.summary: A Chrome MV3 extension for the owner's Base and Solana money: **holdings, profit and loss, pool discovery, backtests and strategy changes, swap quotes, and alerts** when a more profitable pool or strategy appears. It also keeps an **experimental grid trading strategy on Jupiter (Solana)** with

files.name: fake-soltui-host.mjs
files.title: fake-soltui-host
files.summary: Speaks Chrome's native messaging framing on stdio, over the fake registry. SOLTUI_FAKE_MODE: hang (never answers) | crash (exits at once) | garbage (bad frame).

files.name: fake-soltui-registry.js
files.title: fake-soltui-registry
files.summary: A stand-in for soltui's registry with the same envelope shapes as the contract. It exists so the extension's side of the bridge is tested without Python; the real host is exercised in tools/e2e.mjs.

files.name: cdp.mjs
files.title: cdp
files.summary: Minimal Chrome DevTools Protocol client over the DevTools pipe. Why the pipe and not a WebSocket: `Extensions.loadUnpacked` is only exposed on `--remote-debugging-pipe` (with `--enable-unsafe-extension-debugging`), and the branded Chrome channel ignores `--load-extension`. So this needs Chrome for Testing or Chromium, and it needs no port, no HTTP discovery and no package.

files.name: guard.mjs
files.title: guard
files.summary: What the e2e harness may ask the extension to do. The harness drives the real service worker through `chrome.runtime.sendMessage`. It must never arm the extension, change its mode, create a key or cancel an order, so every message goes through this allowlist first.

files.name: soltui-host.mjs
files.title: soltui-host
files.summary: The soltui native messaging host, for the real-browser e2e. Chrome for Testing runs with a throwaway --user-data-dir, and Chrome looks for native messaging host manifests in <user-data-dir>/NativeMessagingHosts first.

files.name: manifest.json
files.title: manifest
files.summary: Generated JSON object, 12 keys (manifest_version, name, version, description, minimum_chrome_version, background...).

files.name: package.json
files.title: package
files.summary: Generated JSON object, 8 keys (name, version, private, type, description, bin...).

files.name: service-worker.js
files.title: service-worker
files.summary: MV3 service worker — the extension surface of the command registry. There is no long-lived process here. The worker is woken by an alarm, runs one tick, and is free to die. Nothing may be held in module scope that the next tick depends on: everything durable lives in IndexedDB or chrome.storage.local, and the tick rebuilds its world from those plus the venue's live state.

files.name: soltui-transport.js
files.title: soltui-transport
files.summary: Service-worker transport to the soltui native messaging host. Chrome starts `com.mitchhudson.soltui` (soltui/native_host.py) on demand and speaks length-prefixed JSON with it. This file owns what is Chrome-specific about that: the port, the request id, the per-call timeout and the clean error when the host is not installed.

files.name: alerts.js
files.title: alerts
files.summary: Alerts: "there is a more profitable pool or strategy than what you have now". Pure. No I/O, no chrome.*, no clock of its own: the scan in commands.js reads the inputs, and this file decides.

files.name: autoreload.js
files.title: autoreload
files.summary: Auto-reload on update, as a pure decision with injected effects. Once a minute the service worker asks the soltui host for `buildHash`, a SHA-256 over the manifest and src/ of the extension directory on disk. When that hash differs from the one the worker stored, the code on disk is newer than the code Chrome loaded, and `chrome.runtime.reload()` picks it up. A reload kills the worker.

files.name: commands.js
files.title: commands
files.summary: The command registry — single source of truth for every action this project can perform. Three surfaces drive this one registry: extension src/bg/service-worker.js (chrome.runtime messages) CLI tools/cli.js (argv) HTTP API tools/api-server.js (POST /v1/<command>) Nothing may be reachable from one surface and not the others.

files.name: engine.js
files.title: engine
files.summary: The tick. Order of operations is the whole design: RECONCILE before PLAN, always. A MV3 service worker can be killed at any moment, including between "write the intent" and "the venue accepted the order". So the venue's live order list — not our local records — is the source of truth at the top of every tick. Local state is a cache and a journal, nothing more.

files.name: grid.js
files.title: grid
files.summary: Pure grid-strategy engine. No I/O, no chrome.* APIs, no network. Everything here is a deterministic function of (config, price, open state) so the whole strategy is unit testable and a service-worker restart can recompute intent from scratch.

files.name: pnl.js
files.title: pnl
files.summary: P&L accounting. Two lot-matching modes, because two consumers want different answers: PAIRED (default) A sell fill that records the lots its intent was paired with (`closesLots`) closes THOSE lots. Grid exits are placed one rung above a specific buy, so when rung B's exit fills before rung A's, the inventory still held is A's, and strict FIFO would instead consume A and leave B behind.

files.name: risk.js
files.title: risk
files.summary: Risk rails. Every rail is enforced here, in code, as a gate the executor must pass before anything is submitted. A rail that lives only in the README is not a rail. `evaluate()` is pure so the dashboard can show exactly which rail would block a grid before you arm it.

files.name: soltui.js
files.title: soltui
files.summary: The soltui bridge, transport-free. soltui (Python) owns its own command registry and answers every call with one JSON envelope: {"ok": true, "command": "x.y", "result": <json>, "error": null} {"ok": false, "command": "x.y", "result": null, "error": {"code", "message"}} This module forwards a call to an injected transport and hands that envelope back UNCHANGED, so the extension, the extension's nod

files.name: attribution.js
files.title: attribution
files.summary: Licence-required attribution, in one place. The Jupiter SDK & API License Agreement (read 2026-08-04) imposes two display obligations that are easy for a private tool to miss, because nobody else sees the UI: §8.4 the product "shall prominently display to end users ... 'Powered by Jupiter'".

files.name: http.js
files.title: http
files.summary: HTTP layer for the Jupiter APIs. A grid ticking every 30s across N rungs will hit rate limits on the free tier, so retry/backoff and a per-tick request budget are part of the client rather than something callers remember to add.

files.name: price.js
files.title: price
files.summary: Price lookup. Two shapes have shipped across Price API versions (`{ <mint>: {...} }` in v3, `{ data: { <mint>: {...} } }` in v2). The parser accepts either and throws a named error on anything else, so a version bump surfaces as one clear failure instead of `undefined` propagating into order sizing.

files.name: trigger.js
files.title: trigger
files.summary: Jupiter Trigger V2 client. Endpoint shapes below are transcribed from the live docs (verified 2026-11-06, with contract regression fixtures): https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/create-order https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/authentication https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/deposit https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/manage-orders Flow: authent

files.name: evm.js
files.title: evm
files.summary: The small slice of EVM ABI encoding the market reads need, in BigInt. Kept by hand rather than pulling in viem or ethers: the extension has zero runtime dependencies (CLAUDE.md, house style), and the reads here are a handful of fixed-shape view calls.

files.name: holdings.js
files.title: holdings
files.summary: Live holdings: what the owner's public Base and Solana addresses hold, in USD. Read-only. No key, no signature, no transaction: Base is read with eth_getBalance and ERC-20 balanceOf through one JSON-RPC batch, Solana with getBalance and getTokenAccountsByOwner, prices from DefiLlama (Base) and the keyless Jupiter price API (Solana).

files.name: net.js
files.title: net
files.summary: Read-only network access for the market modules (holdings, pools, quotes). Everything here goes through `request` in src/jupiter/http.js, so the timeout, retry and JSON handling are the same ones the trading path uses. The fetch implementation comes from `deps.fetch`: the service worker, the CLI and the HTTP API inject the platform fetch, and tests inject a stub.

files.name: pools.js
files.title: pools
files.summary: Pool discovery from DefiLlama yields (keyless, https://yields.llama.fi/pools). Every APY here is QUOTED by DefiLlama, not measured by this project. It includes reward emissions and can be a short-window spike.

files.name: quote.js
files.title: quote
files.summary: Swap quotes. Quote only: nothing here builds, signs or sends a transaction. The extension's signer has no semantic transaction verifier, so live signing stays blocked (CLAUDE.md, "Known-unverified areas"). A quote is handed to the venue's own page, where the owner reviews and signs in their wallet. See Stele KNOW-837.

files.name: tokens.js
files.title: tokens
files.summary: Chains, endpoints and the known-token lists the market reads use. Base: chain id 8453 (0x2105), public RPC https://mainnet.base.org (docs.base.org network table), with base-rpc.publicnode.com first because soltui/wallet.py found it less throttled. Since Denim (Base mainnet, 2026-11-05) the `pending` tag no longer returns preconfirmation state, so every read here uses `latest`.

files.name: fileStore.js
files.title: fileStore
files.summary: Node-side persistence, API-compatible with the browser surfaces. The CLI and HTTP API need the same durability the extension gets from IndexedDB + chrome.storage.local, so this provides: FileStore the Store API (intents, fills, carry, events) on a JSON file createFileArea a chrome.storage.local-shaped {get,set} on a JSON file, so ConfigStore works unchanged outside the browser Writes go through a

files.name: memoryStore.js
files.title: memoryStore
files.summary: In-memory Store, API-compatible with the IndexedDB one. Exists so the tick can run headless — under `node --test` and in tools/dryrun.js — without Chrome or a fake IndexedDB. The engine takes its store as a dependency precisely so this substitution is possible.

files.name: store.js
files.title: store
files.summary: Persistence. Two surfaces, chosen by what the data is: chrome.storage.local — config and limits. Small, synchronously readable at worker start, and NEVER `.sync` (that would push settings, and anything near them, to Google's servers). IndexedDB — the intent journal and fill log.

files.name: charts.js
files.title: charts
files.summary: Charts drawn with TradingView Lightweight Charts, the one vendored runtime library (extension/vendor/lightweight-charts/, Apache-2.0, pinned 5.2.1). The library is imported lazily, on first draw, so node tests and the service worker never load it, and a missing or broken copy degrades to the caller's SVG fallback instead of a blank panel.

files.name: dashboard.js
files.title: dashboard
files.summary: Dashboard shell: hash routing between views, the top bar, the stored scan, and Settings. Views load on first visit and on their own Refresh buttons; Overview paints from the stored scan first so the page is useful before any network answers. Every action goes through a registry command (src/core/commands.js) — this page holds no trading or alert logic of its own.

files.name: popup.js
files.title: popup
files.summary: Popup: holdings and alerts at a glance, shortcuts into the dashboard, and the grid's arm / disarm / kill controls (collapsed: the grid is experimental). All state comes from the service worker over messages. The popup holds no strategy logic — it can be closed mid-tick without consequence, and it must never be the thing that decides whether an order is placed.

files.name: session-key-form.js
files.title: session-key-form
files.summary: Pure helpers for the dashboard's "Create session key" control. Kept free of DOM and chrome.* so the input rules and the message shape are unit-testable. The command in src/core/commands.js stays the authority; this only catches a typo before a passphrase is sealed into a vault that nothing can reopen.

files.name: soltui-panel.js
files.title: soltui-panel
files.summary: Dashboard panel for the soltui command bridge. The command list comes from the registry (`soltuiCommands`), the form is built from each command's declared params by type, and a Run sends only `soltuiCall` with a command name taken from that list. Nothing here knows a soltui command by name, so a new soltui command shows up with no change.

files.name: ui-kit.js
files.title: ui-kit
files.summary: Shared helpers for the dashboard views: DOM building, number formatting, tables, chips and a small SVG line chart. Every string that reaches the page goes through textContent or a DOM attribute, never innerHTML. Token names, pool symbols, venue errors and soltui output are third-party data, and these pages hold extension privileges (KNOW-407): one missed escape would be XSS with real reach.

files.name: view-grid.js
files.title: view-grid
files.summary: Grid view: the Jupiter ladder grid's configuration, risk rails, journal and P&L. Moved off the front page in the 0.3.0 redesign because the strategy loses to buy-and-hold walk-forward (Stele KNOW-605); the behaviour is unchanged. The equity curve is drawn with the vendored Lightweight Charts library (src/ui/charts.js; local file, because MV3 forbids remote code).

files.name: view-markets.js
files.title: view-markets
files.summary: Holdings, Profit & loss and Discover views. Holdings come from the extension's own read-only market reads (holdings); the deeper scan, snapshots, P&L history and the Aero scout come from soltui. Every figure keeps its source label: a quoted APY is never shown as income.

files.name: view-overview.js
files.title: view-overview
files.summary: Overview and Alerts views. The overview paints from the stored scan first (instant, no network), then refreshes holdings live. Alerts come from the background scan (scanAlerts, src/core/alerts.js); this page only shows and acknowledges them.

files.name: view-trade.js
files.title: view-trade
files.summary: Backtest & strategies and Swap views. Strategy work runs in soltui (the backtester is Python): Top 5 evidence, the roster, CPCV sweeps and signal defaults. Swaps are quotes from the extension's registry (swapQuote); signing happens on the venue page (Stele KNOW-837).

files.name: wallet-pubkey.js
files.title: wallet-pubkey
files.summary: "Use soltui Solana address": fill the Wallet pubkey field from the address saved in soltui. The address comes through the same bridge as every other soltui call: the page sends `soltuiCall` for the read-only `wallet.addresses` command, which returns the public Solana and EVM addresses and nothing else (never an extended public key, never key material).

files.name: index.js
files.title: index
files.summary: Venue layer. The grid engine is venue-agnostic: it emits intents, and a venue adapter turns them into orders. That seam exists because the two candidate venues on Jupiter are in very different states of readiness: Trigger V2 — REST, returns signable transactions. Live-capable today. SPOT. Perps — NO public REST write API as of 2026-08-04.

files.name: triggerVenue.js
files.title: triggerVenue
files.summary: Jupiter Trigger V2 venue adapter. Live writes require a trusted semantic-verification signing bridge. The bundled raw session-key signer does not provide one, so it cannot sign remote-crafted money movements. A grid is a ladder of resting price orders, which is exactly what this API is for, and V2 keeps pending orders off-chain so the ladder is not a public roadmap for front-runners.

files.name: signer.js
files.title: signer
files.summary: Signing. Three honest modes, because "unattended bot" and "wallet popup per trade" are mutually exclusive and pretending otherwise ships a broken default: DRY_RUN nothing is ever signed. The signer throws if asked. SEMI_AUTO the worker prepares the transaction and queues it; a human approves each one in the dashboard. Safe, not unattended.

files.name: solana.js
files.title: solana
files.summary: Minimal Solana wire-format helpers. Hand-rolled instead of pulling in @solana/web3.js because the extension needs exactly two things — base58 and inserting a signature into an already-built transaction — and shipping a megabyte of bundled dependencies into a service worker for that is a poor trade. The transaction itself is always built by Jupiter; we never construct instructions.

files.name: e2e-harness.test.js
files.title: e2e-harness.test
files.summary: The browser e2e (tools/e2e.mjs) cannot run under `node --test`: it needs Chrome for Testing. What can be tested without a browser is the part that makes it safe.

files.name: version.test.js
files.title: version.test
files.summary: The manifest version is what the owner sees in chrome://extensions and in the popup header. A change that ships without bumping it looks like no change at all (2026-11-07: the SolTUI panel shipped as 0.1.0 and read as "nothing changed"). CI also fails a pull request that edits src/ or manifest.json without bumping the version; this test keeps the two version fields in step.

files.name: api-server.js
files.title: api-server
files.summary: HTTP API surface. Routes are generated from the registry in src/core/commands.js — the same registry the CLI and the extension use — so no endpoint can drift from the extension's behaviour.

files.name: cli.js

files.summary: Audit -- and optionally repair -- gaps in Coinbase 1m candle data using ticks. Why this exists. files.name: README.md
files.title: soltui — SOL strategy console
files.summary: A sixteen-tab Textual TUI plus a macOS menu-bar indicator over the backtester. Structured like `~/dev/net-dns-monitor`: pure, tested logic modules with a thin wiring shell.

files.name: analyze.py
files.title: research/ is not a package, so `research.decide` is not importable without the
files.summary: What every strategy, signal and indicator said about one coin at one moment. Pure logic behind the Analyze tab. No Textual import, no widget. ## It wraps `research/decide.py`; it does not reimplement it `decide.py`'s one substantive guarantee is that the exposures it reports are the numbers the engine would have acted on.

files.name: api.py
files.title: api
files.summary: HTTP surface: `soltui api [--port N]`. Stdlib `http.server`; mirrors extension/tools/api-server.js. GET /v1/health liveness, no auth GET /v1/commands the `list` envelope GET /v1/<command>?a=1 read-only commands, args from the query string POST /v1/<command> any command, args from a JSON object body Command routes return the registry envelope exactly as `commands.dumps` renders it, so the body is b

files.name: app.py
files.title: app
files.summary: macOS menu-bar shell. Thin by design. python3 -m soltui.app Mirrors `netdnsmonitor/app.py`: every decision lives in already-tested modules (`status`, `config`, `roster`, `runner`), and this file only wires them to a `rumps.Timer` and a status-item title.

files.name: bgcontrol.py
files.title: Where the liveness lock lives, and the variable that tells a spawned worker the
files.summary: Start, stop and inspect the background sweep process. Separated from `bgqueue` (which is pure logic) and from `bgworker` (which is the work) because process lifecycle is the part with the OS-specific behaviour, and keeping it in one small module is what lets the other two stay testable.

files.name: bgqueue.py
files.title: Where the worker and the TUI meet. Under the existing config dir rather than a
files.summary: Job queue for the background backtest sweep. Pure logic; no UI, no processes. The TUI's own sweep (`runner.py`) evaluates the roster and blocks a thread until it finishes.

files.name: bgworker.py
files.title: The nicest a process can ask to be. Set unconditionally at startup rather than
files.summary: The background backtest worker: a separate, low-priority process. python3 -m soltui.bgworker --asset SOL python3 -m soltui.bgworker --asset SOL --horizons medium --max-tier 1 --limit 50 Run directly it is a normal foreground script; the TUI launches it through `bgcontrol.start()`, which is what applies the background scheduling policy.

files.name: soltui
files.title: soltui launcher: `soltui` opens the console from anywhere.

files.name: bots.py
files.title: The representative grids auto-optimize searches. Small on purpose: every extra configuration is
files.summary: The Bots tab: grid, triangular-arbitrage and DCA bots. Backtest, forward test, auto-optimize. Every bot here is a simulation. Nothing in this module places an order, holds a key or talks to a venue's trading API; the only network reads are public market data (the recorded Coinbase stream in `pricefeed`, and Coinbase candles for the triangle candle proxy).

files.name: bots_screens.py
files.title: bots_screens
files.summary: The Bots tab's two pop-up windows: the coin picker and the auto-optimize window. Presentation only, like `help_screen.py`. Neither window runs a command itself: the coin picker returns the chosen coins to the tab, and the auto-optimize window shows what the tab's worker reports (`bots.progress` while it runs, the `bots.optimize` result when it ends).

files.name: cli.py
files.title: cli
files.summary: Command-line surface: `soltui call <name> [--param k=v ...] [--json '{...}']` and `soltui list`. Prints the registry envelope (`commands.dumps`) on stdout, one line, and exits 0 when `ok` else 1. No logic of its own: parsing arguments into params is all it does; `dispatch` does the rest, including the call log.

files.name: commands.py
files.title: The research scripts import pandas and numpy, so they must run on the interpreter running this
files.summary: The soltui command registry: one set of calls for the TUI, CLI, HTTP API and native host. Every action the console can take is a registered `Command`. Every surface goes through `dispatch(name, params, surface)`, which validates parameters, applies the confirm gate, runs the handler, wraps the outcome in the response envelope and appends one line to the call log.

files.name: compound.py
files.title: With adaptive weighting on, the fetched bars give each metric its track record even before the
files.summary: Compound five-minute tester: saved configuration, live reads, forward ledger, sweeps. python3 -m soltui.compound signal --asset SOL # score now, explain every metric python3 -m soltui.compound forward --asset SOL --loop # record a call per closed 5m bar python3 -m soltui.compound status --asset SOL # forward-test hit rates python3 -m soltui.compound backtest --asset SOL # compound + each component

files.name: compound_agent.py
files.title: compound_agent
files.summary: Install, remove or inspect the compound 5m autopilot LaunchAgent. python -m soltui.compound_agent install [--python P] [--repo R] [--no-start] python -m soltui.compound_agent uninstall python -m soltui.compound_agent status The job is `com.mitchhudson.soltui.compound-autopilot`: every five minutes (and once at load) it runs `python -m soltui.compound autopilot` from the repo root.

files.name: config.py
files.title: SOLTUI_CONFIG_DIR exists so tests and the bridge parity suite never touch the owner's real config.
files.summary: Settings load/save for the TUI. Pure logic; no UI, no I/O beyond one file. Config lives at `~/.config/soltui/config.yaml`, following the same convention as `netdnsmonitor`. YAML is optional at runtime -- if PyYAML is missing the app falls back to JSON at the same path with a `.json` suffix, so a missing optional dependency degrades rather than crashes.

files.name: cumulative.py
files.title: The project's own evidence floor, matching `MIN_RANKABLE_TRADES` in
files.summary: Aggregate every committed backtest result — with the evidence floor applied. Pure logic behind the Cumulative tab. No Textual import, no widget. ## The defect this module is built to avoid `cpcv_evaluate` marks a configuration `insufficient` when it falls below `min_total_trades`, prints it **DROPPED**, and **still returns a full path count**.

files.name: docs_browser.py
files.title: Refuse to load a file larger than this into a viewer widget. The largest tracked
files.summary: Read-only catalogue and file reader behind the Docs tab. Pure logic: no Textual import, no widget, no I/O beyond reading files the catalogue already lists. That split is what lets this be tested without driving a terminal, and it matches `config.py`, `roster.py` and the other modules the TUI sits on.

files.name: eth_scan.py
files.title: (contract, symbol, decimals, Coinbase symbol to price it with or None). Symbols and decimals were
files.summary: Ethereum mainnet (L1) holdings of one public address: native ETH plus a well-known token list. `base_address` in Settings is the same EVM key viewed on Base; `eth_address` is the mainnet view. Reads only: `eth_getBalance` and `balanceOf` over public JSON-RPC, USD prices from Coinbase. There is no indexer here, so a token that is not in `TOKENS` is not discovered, and the scan says so.

files.name: forwardtest.py
files.title: forwardtest
files.summary: Prospective, paper-only trials of registered strategies on closed Coinbase minutes.

files.name: hdwallet.py
files.title: -- secp256k1 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
files.summary: Public-key-only BIP32 derivation and address encoding. Stdlib only, no private keys anywhere. An extended PUBLIC key (xpub and its SLIP-132 cousins) is enough to derive every receive and change address of a wallet, so the console can watch a wallet without ever holding anything that can spend.

files.name: help.py
files.title: Define the unit and an example before the statistical qualification. A green
files.summary: Plain-language help shared by hover tooltips and the F1 reference.

files.name: help_screen.py
files.title: help_screen
files.summary: Keyboard-accessible, scrollable counterpart of the hover help.

files.name: liquidity.py
files.title: How often the tab re-reads the files, and how old `generated_at` may get
files.summary: Liquidity tab logic: read the Aero LP daemon's state files, format them. Pure, stdlib-only, and read-only with one exception. The liquidity daemon (`liquidity/`, `aero-lp daemon`) writes `status.json` and `scout.json`; this module only reads them. The single write is the `KILL` switch file, which `set_kill()` creates or deletes. The contract is `liquidity/STATE_FILES.md`.

files.name: live_run.py
files.title: live_run

files.title: Solana brand colours.

A finely detailed tree becomes mush there.

files.name: menubar_launcher.py
files.title: In an alias build this file lives in the source tree, so the repo root is its
files.summary: py2app entry point for the menu-bar app. ## Why this file exists py2app executes its target as a **top-level script**, not as a module inside a package.

files.name: native_host.py
files.title: native_host
files.summary: Chrome native-messaging host `com.mitchhudson.soltui`: the extension's door into the registry. Speaks Chrome's framing on stdio: a 4-byte little-endian length, then that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON. It serves many requests per connection (`connectNative`) or one (`sendNativeMessage`).

files.name: native_host_install.py
files.title: Browser user-data directories under ~/Library/Application Support that take a NativeMessagingHosts dir.
files.summary: Install, remove or inspect the native-messaging host registration. python -m soltui.native_host_install install [--python P] [--repo R] [--extra-id ID ...] [--dir D ...] python -m soltui.native_host_install uninstall python -m soltui.native_host_install status `install` writes an executable wrapper (absolute paths, no arguments, which is what Chrome requires of a manifest `path`) that runs the con

files.name: netpct.py
files.title: netpct
files.summary: Net percentage growth or decline, always with the word that names its source. One definition for every results view: `final / initial - 1`, as a signed fraction. A bare "+9.4%" reads as "my money is up", and most figures in this package are simulations, so the text form never leaves the source word off.

files.name: paper.py
files.title: Stated in the UI so the mode is never ambiguous.
files.summary: Dry-run simulator for the Execute tab. ## Why this is a replay and not a live loop The obvious design -- step forward bar by bar and compute fills as you go -- would create a SECOND order-execution path alongside `backtester/core/engine.py`.

files.name: pnl.py
files.title: Which sources are simulations and which are real money. A dry-run liquidity daemon is simulated;
files.summary: Profit and loss over a variable window: the maths behind the P&L tab. Pure functions over plain data, so every figure can be checked with a fixture and no event loop, network or price file.

files.name: portfolio.py
files.title: -- changes -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
files.summary: Portfolio monitoring: timestamped per-chain snapshots, the changes between them, and a notice line. A snapshot is one line of `snapshots.jsonl` under `~/Library/Application Support/soltui/portfolio/` (mode 600). It holds per-chain balances by symbol, a USD value, the prices used and the script types an xpub scan found.

files.name: portfolio_agent.py
files.title: portfolio_agent
files.summary: Install, remove or inspect the hourly portfolio-snapshot LaunchAgent. python -m soltui.portfolio_agent install [--python P] [--repo R] [--no-start] python -m soltui.portfolio_agent uninstall python -m soltui.portfolio_agent status The job is `com.mitchhudson.soltui.portfolio`: once an hour (and once at load) it runs `python -m soltui.cli call portfolio.snapshot` from the repo root, so it goes thro

files.name: presets.py
files.title: presets
files.summary: The Top 5 configurations as ready-to-use presets for Analyze, Live Run and Execute. `top5.py` reads the committed evidence; this module turns each row into something a tab can apply with one click, from one place, so every surface (TUI, CLI, API, extension) sees the same list.

files.name: pricefeed.py
files.title: Used when the products endpoint cannot be reached: the markets Coinbase listed on 2026-11-08
files.summary: Streaming coin prices: the public Coinbase Exchange `ticker` channel, recorded to disk. python -m soltui.pricefeed record # the recorder loop (the console starts it detached) python -m soltui.pricefeed status # what is recorded, and the latest prices Before this module the console polled prices (Coinbase REST spot, closed 5m candles) and kept nothing between bars.

files.name: reference.py
files.title: The Research tab's content. Kept here as data rather than fetched or computed:
files.summary: Static reference content for the Research and Signals tabs. Kept out of `tui.py` so the command registry (`research.get`, `signals.reference`) can serve the same data to every surface without importing Textual.

files.title: roster
files.summary: The user's strategy roster: which strategies are active, with what parameters. Backs the Strategies tab. Kept pure so add/remove is testable without a UI. Two invariants worth stating, because both prevent a class of confusing failure later rather than at the point of the mistake: 1.

files.name: runner.py
files.title: runner
files.summary: Background sweep runner. Turns a roster into results while keeping the UI live. The menu-bar indicator and the Backtest tab both need "how much is left", which means the sweep has to report progress as it goes rather than blocking until done. This module owns that: a worker thread, a progress callback, and a cancellation flag.

files.name: serve.py
files.title: The command textual-serve runs as a subprocess. Absolute interpreter and an
files.summary: Serve the Textual console as a real window, without needing a TTY. python3 -m soltui.serve # then open the printed URL python3 -m soltui.serve --port 8899 --no-open ## Why this exists The console has had five tabs, buttons and settings since it was written — but the only way to reach them was `app.py`'s "Open TUI" menu item, which does: tell application "Terminal" to do script "cd <repo> && python

files.name: setup_app.py
files.title: LSUIElement False on purpose: net-dns-monitor's bundle shows in the Dock, and
files.summary: py2app build for the soltui menu-bar app. cd /Users/mitch.hudson/dev/solmargintrader python3 soltui/setup_app.py py2app -A # alias build (recommended, see below) ## Why alias mode A full py2app freeze would have to embed pandas and numpy, which the backtester imports. That is slow, large, and a well-known source of missing-dylib breakage.

files.name: signals.py
files.title: Which defaults map to which strategy constructor kwargs. Explicit rather than
files.summary: Editable signal parameters: the tunables behind the Signals tab. ## The model, because it needs to be unambiguous A *signal* is an indicator with a period or threshold (RSI's period, Bollinger's width, MACD's spans). A *strategy* is a rule built on one or more signals. The same signal is shared by several strategies -- `rsi` and any composite containing it both read the RSI period.

files.name: soltui-service
files.title: py2app's launcher loads libpython from the paths in Info.plist PyRuntimeLocations, which it

files.name: spot_prices.py
files.title: spot_prices
files.summary: USD spot prices from Coinbase's public endpoint (no key). A price it cannot give is None, never 0. `https://api.coinbase.com/v2/prices/<SYMBOL>-USD/spot` answers `{"data": {"amount": "76021.455"}}`. A symbol Coinbase does not list answers an error body; that, a network failure and a non-positive or non-finite amount all become None, so the caller reports the value as unknown instead of as zero.

files.name: status.py
files.title: Leading glyphs. Kept ASCII-ish and narrow: a macOS status item has very little
files.summary: Pure menu-bar title logic, kept out of the rumps shell so it is testable without a real macOS event loop. Mirrors `netdnsmonitor/status.py`: one pure `build_title()` the app calls every tick, plus the state it reads.

files.name: __init__.py
files.title: __init__
files.summary: soltui tests. The suite must never read or write the owner's real state, so the directories soltui resolves at import time are pointed at a throwaway tree before any soltui module is imported (this package is imported first by `unittest discover -s soltui/tests -t .`). Individual tests that need a clean slate create their own directories and patch the module constants.

files.name: bridge_support.py
files.title: Commands that run for minutes, spawn processes, hit the network or write repo files. The parity suite
files.summary: Shared fixtures for the command-bridge tests: an isolated world and the four surface runners.

files.name: base_recorded.json
files.title: base_recorded

files.name: test_bgcontrol.py
files.title: test_bgcontrol
files.summary: Tests for the background worker's process lifecycle. Two of these exist because the bug they describe actually shipped in an earlier draft of this module and only turned up when the worker was spawned for real: `taskpolicy` lives in /usr/sbin rather than /usr/bin, and the pidfile was written by the child late enough that Stop-after-Start found nothing to signal.

files.name: test_bgcontrol_identity.py
files.title: test_bgcontrol_identity
files.summary: Stop addresses a temporary worker instance, never a recorded process id.

files.name: test_bgqueue.py
files.title: test_bgqueue
files.summary: Tests for the background sweep's queue, file contract and leaderboard. The properties worth defending here are the ones a background process makes hard to notice going wrong: an ordering that stops putting the published preset first, a resume that re-runs finished work, a reader that dies on a torn line, and — most importantly — a leaderboard that quietly ranks a Sharpe computed from three trades.

files.name: test_bgworker.py
files.title: test_bgworker
files.summary: Tests for the background worker's run loop. `run()` takes its results path, state path, settings and stop flag as arguments precisely so the loop can be driven without spawning a process or touching real price data — the strategy evaluation itself is patched out, because what is under test here is the *loop*: resume, stop, limit, and the failure paths.

files.name: test_bgworker_audit.py
files.title: test_bgworker_audit
files.summary: Offline regression cases for provenance, lock handoff, and job budgets.

files.name: test_bots.py
files.title: test_bots
files.summary: The Bots tab's engine: configs, data, backtests, forward tests and the auto-optimize gate. No network and no real price data: bars come from `SyntheticLoader` written to a temporary data directory, and recorded snapshots are written to a temporary prices directory.

files.name: test_bridge_buttons.py
files.title: test_bridge_buttons
files.summary: Every TUI button is a registry command: a new button cannot skip the registry.

files.name: test_bridge_parity.py
files.title: test_bridge_parity
files.summary: One registry, four surfaces: the same call returns the same envelope bytes everywhere. Driven by the registry itself, so a command added tomorrow is covered the day it is registered (the way extension/test/surfaces.test.js covers the extension's registry).

files.name: test_bridge_surfaces.py
files.title: test_bridge_surfaces
files.summary: Access, framing, logging and install behaviour of the command bridge.

files.name: test_compound.py
files.title: test_compound
files.summary: Compound five-minute tester: saved config, live reads, forward ledger, and the tab.

files.name: test_docs_browser.py
files.title: test_docs_browser
files.summary: Tests for the Docs tab's editing guards. The load-bearing assertions are the refusals: a file under `research/results/` or not in the catalogue must never be writable, regardless of what the caller claims about it. Those are the properties a UI bug could silently violate, so they are asserted directly rather than left to code review.

files.name: test_docs_search.py
files.title: test_docs_search
files.summary: Docs-tab index search: the `docs.search` commands and the lazy loading around them. The memory claim is the point: the keyword postings, the embedding matrix and the ~670 MB embedding model must not be loaded until someone searches, and must be releasable. Ollama and the idle indexer are patched out; nothing here embeds anything or starts a process.

files.name: test_eth_scan.py
files.title: test_eth_scan
files.summary: Ethereum mainnet scan: native ETH, the built-in token list, Coinbase prices, partial results.

files.name: test_forwardtest.py
files.title: test_forwardtest
files.summary: Prospective evidence, horizon isolation, and the roster keyboard workflow.

files.name: test_hdwallet.py
files.title: BIP32 test vector 2 (master) and its first non-hardened child; vector 1 m/0H and its child m/0H/1.
files.summary: BIP32 public derivation, address encoding and the refusal of private keys, on published test vectors. Every key here is a public test vector from BIP32 or BIP84, or is built in the test from filler bytes. None is a real wallet.

files.name: test_help.py
files.title: test_help
files.summary: Exercise help discovery and keyboard/mouse access without invoking actions.

files.name: test_launcher.py
files.title: test_launcher
files.summary: The `soltui` shell launcher (soltui/bin/soltui). A fake interpreter stands in for Python, so these tests check the launcher's own job — find the repo through a symlink, cd there, pick the module, pass arguments through — without starting Textual.

files.name: test_liquidity.py
files.title: test_liquidity
files.summary: The Liquidity tab: loader tolerance, formatting, summary math, KILL toggle. The logic is in `soltui.liquidity` (pure); the last class mounts the real app against a fixture state dir. Fixtures follow `liquidity/STATE_FILES.md`. The load-bearing test is `test_every_percentage_column_carries_a_source_word`: a bare "+4.6%" under a header with no source reads as "my money is up".

files.name: test_panes.py
files.title: test_panes
files.summary: The four modules behind the new console tabs. No test here drives a terminal, opens a socket, or reads `data/`. That is the same split the rest of this package keeps: `tui.py` is presentation, and the logic lives in modules that can be tested without an event loop. The two worth reading first are `test_a_below_floor_row_is_never_rankable` and `test_slicing_happens_before_the_replay`.

files.name: test_pnl.py
files.title: test_pnl
files.summary: The P&L maths, on fixtures: window edges, costs, realized vs unrealized, drawdown, the no-data case. No test here reads a price file, a state file or the network. The numbers are small round ones so each expected value can be checked by hand.

files.name: test_portfolio.py
files.title: test_portfolio
files.summary: Snapshots, balance changes, the notice line, the wallet value curve and the hourly LaunchAgent plist.

files.name: test_presets_netpct.py
files.title: test_presets_netpct
files.summary: Top 5 presets, the net % helper, and the P&L commands end to end on synthetic data. No price file, state file or network: the series is `SyntheticLoader`, the Top 5 evidence is a temp CSV, the liquidity home and journal are temp paths.

files.name: test_pricefeed.py
files.title: test_pricefeed
files.summary: The streaming price recorder: RFC 6455 framing, the handshake, books, snapshots and files. No network: every socket here is a fake, and every file lives in a temporary directory.

files.name: test_service.py
files.title: soltui-service imports the private macos-launchd-supervisor package and exits without it. CI cannot clone
files.summary: Tests for `soltui-service`, the LaunchAgent manager. The script is dash-named so that it reads as a command rather than a module, which means it cannot be imported normally; it is loaded by path below. What these cover is one failure that cost a debugging session: the agent plist sitting on disk while launchd knows nothing about it.

files.title: soltui-service imports the private macos-launchd-supervisor package and exits without it. CI cannot clone

files.name: test_signals.py
files.title: test_signals
files.summary: Tests for editable signal parameters. The load-bearing property: **an explicit per-entry parameter always beats a signal default.** Getting that direction backwards would mean the Signals tab silently overwrites a value the user deliberately pinned in the Strategies tab, and the symptom would be a strategy quietly not doing what its own label says.

files.name: test_status_roster.py
files.title: test_status_roster
files.summary: Tests for the pure soltui layer: indicator title, settings, roster, replay. The load-bearing assertion in this file is that **no money figure in the menu-bar title is ever unlabelled**. A naked '+9.4%' in a status bar reads as a live account balance, and there is no live account. That property is asserted directly rather than left to code review.

files.name: test_strategy_history.py
files.title: test_strategy_history
files.summary: The Strategies tab's test history and its three Backtest buttons. History is derived from the background sweep's results file, so what it can get wrong is counting and choosing: a duplicate line counted as a second test, a best-of-many row shown as "the" result, an untestable strategy shown as merely untested, a button that starts a sweep that has nothing to do. Each test targets one of those.

files.name: test_top5.py
files.title: test_top5
files.summary: Tests for the Top 5 tab's pure module. The load-bearing assertions: the module reads the committed evidence file faithfully (ranks, home rows, transfers), never turns absent evidence into a zero, and recovers composite members from labels without a duplicated name-to-members table that could drift from research/cross_asset_cpcv.py.

files.name: test_tui.py
files.title: Terminal big enough that every button is on-screen; Pilot.click() raises
files.summary: Smoke tests for the Textual app, driven through Textual's own test harness. An app that imports cleanly but explodes on mount is not working, so these actually mount it, click things, and assert on widget state. `run_test()` runs a headless terminal, so no TTY is required and this is safe in CI.

files.summary: The five recommended configurations, read from the committed evidence. Pure logic behind the Top 5 tab. No Textual import, no widget, and — like `cumulative.py` — no re-computation: this reads what the research drivers wrote and cannot disagree with `verify_numbers.py`.

files.name: tui.py
files.title: Rows the Docs table renders at once. The repo has ~470 tracked files; leave headroom.
files.summary: Textual TUI: the console over the backtester. python3 -m soltui.tui Tabs: Settings, Strategies, Signals, Backtest, Top 5, Execute (dry-run only), Analyze, Cumulative, Research, Docs. All decisions live in the pure modules (`config`, `roster`, `runner`, `paper`, `status`); this file is presentation and wiring.

files.name: utxo_scan.py
files.title: utxo_scan
files.summary: Watch a Bitcoin, Litecoin or Dogecoin wallet from its extended PUBLIC key. Read-only, keyless. The xpub is turned into addresses on this machine (`hdwallet`). Only addresses are sent to the public explorers, never the xpub, and the derived addresses are never logged, printed or returned: a result carries counts and balances only. ## How a wallet is found * Chains 0 (receive) and 1 (change).
